codeReview.summary: The linter and tests cover all requested rule categories, but there are correctness issues that produce false undefined-role errors and can suppress missing-success-criteria warnings.

issues.description: `delegateToPattern` captures any token after `delegate ... to`, so natural text like `Maybe delegate this work to another role.` is parsed as role name `another` and then raised as an undefined role error. This creates false-positive lint failures for vague-language cases that do not actually name a role template.

`lintMissingSuccessCriteria` uses a substring signal check (`hasAnySignal`) and treats the phrase `completion criteria` as sufficient evidence. Prompts that merely mention `completion criteria` (without defining what completion means) bypass the warning, which violates the requirement to flag missing clear success criteria.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill prescribes tests-first with an explicit red phase, but this run's transcript skeleton shows implementation patching before the first targeted test execution. The skill procedure appears stricter than actual execution practice.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: worker-transcripts.jsonl entry for session 28489226-016e-4f98-9f80-31e84b41fec0 shows `ApplyPatch` calls before the first `go test ./internal/promptstack -run TestLint ...` command.

summary: Review failed: prompt-stack-lint broadly implements requested lint rules and tests, but two blocking rule-quality issues remain (false undefined-role detection and overly permissive success-criteria detection).
